data.name: Binay
data.gender_notes: Binay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Binay is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Bina' meaning 'without' and 'Vidyam' meaning 'knowledge'. This name signifies a son who is born without the need for knowledge, as he embodies it himself. In Hindu mythology, Binay is often associated with the god Vishnu, who is the preserver of knowledge and wisdom. The name Binay carries the meaning “Son of Wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Binay usually hope their child will grow to embody son of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the embodiment of wisdom and knowledge
data.etymology: Binay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Binay total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Binay Sen, a Bengali poet, was born on 25 November 1918 in a village called Bibarghat in the Midnapore district of West Bengal, India. He is best known for his works in the genres of modernism and humanism. His poetry was deeply influenced by the Bengal Renaissance and the Indian independence movement. He was a key figure in the Indian literary world during the mid-20th century and passed away on 18 February 1984.
historical_references.context: Bengali poetry, Indian independence movement, Indian literary world

historical_references.reference: Binayak Sen, a renowned human rights activist and physician, was born on 5 July 1947 in Kolkata, India. He is the founder of the People's Committee against Human Rights Violations and the National Human Rights Commission in India. He has been honored with numerous awards including the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1981 and the Padma Shri in 1980 for his work in fighting for the rights of the marginalized and oppressed. He was abducted and brutally murdered by ultranationalist terrorists on 24 January 1997.
historical_references.context: Human rights activism, fighting for the rights of the marginalized and oppressed
